summary: Eribulin mesylate is a non-taxane, halichondrin-class microtubule inhibitor given intravenously, indicated for metastatic breast cancer after at least two prior chemotherapy regimens (including an anthracycline and a taxane) and for unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen. The dose is 1.4 mg/m2 IV over 2-5 minutes on Days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle, reduced for hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A 1.1, B 0.7 mg/m2) and for moderate-to-severe renal impairment (CrCl 15-49: 1.1 mg/m2). Key toxicities are neutropenia (including febrile neutropenia), peripheral neuropathy, QT prolongation and embryo-fetal harm. No clinically meaningful CYP3A4/P-gp drug interactions are expected. It must not be mixed with or given through dextrose-containing solutions.
indications: Treatment of patients with metastatic breast cancer who have previously received at least two chemotherapeutic regimens for metastatic disease (prior anthracycline and taxane in the adjuvant or metastatic setting)
Treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma who have received a prior anthracycline-containing regimen

moa: Eribulin is a synthetic analogue of halichondrin B that inhibits the growth phase of microtubules without affecting the shortening phase and sequesters tubulin into nonproductive aggregates. This tubulin-based antimitotic action causes G2/M cell-cycle block, disruption of mitotic spindles, and apoptotic cell death after prolonged mitotic blockage. It also alters tumor vasculature, reducing hypoxia, and decreases migration and invasiveness of breast cancer cells in vitro.

absolute: No contraindications are listed in the product labeling
monitor: Complete blood count before each dose
ECG/QT and serum electrolytes (potassium, magnesium, calcium)

preg: Can cause fetal harm based on animal data and mechanism of action; eribulin caused increased abortion and severe fetal malformations in rats at doses below the recommended human dose. No human data. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for an appropriate period afterward, and advise pregnant women of the risk to the fetus.
lact: There are no data on the presence of eribulin in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for an appropriate period after the last dose.
renal: For moderate or severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance 15-49 mL/min), reduce the dose to 1.1 mg/m2. No reduction is required for mild renal impairment.
hepatic: Reduce the dose for hepatic impairment: Child-Pugh A to 1.1 mg/m2 and Child-Pugh B to 0.7 mg/m2. Eribulin has not been studied in severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment.

major: Other QT-prolonging drugs - additive risk of QT prolongation and arrhythmia; monitor ECG and electrolytes
moderate: Other neurotoxic agents - additive peripheral neuropathy
minor: No clinically meaningful interaction expected with CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers or P-gp inhibitors
interactions.diagnostics: May cause neutropenia, anemia, hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, raised liver enzymes, and QT prolongation on ECG.

serious: Severe neutropenia and febrile neutropenia (can be fatal)

monitoring: Complete blood count before each dose (and more often if cytopenic)
ECG/QT and serum electrolytes (correct potassium and magnesium) in at-risk patients
Pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential before starting
counsel: This chemotherapy is given as a short injection on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle
Your blood counts will be checked before each dose - report fever or signs of infection urgently
Tell the team about numbness, tingling or weakness in hands and feet
Hair loss, tiredness, nausea and constipation are common
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed; tell your doctor if you may be pregnant
pk: Acts during cell division (G2/M block); clinical antitumor effect over cycles
Reached at end of the short IV infusion; linear pharmacokinetics
No accumulation with weekly (Day 1/8) dosing; eliminated mainly unchanged in feces
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); do not freeze; keep in original carton
pearls: Dose schedule is Days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle - not weekly continuous
Reduce dose for hepatic (Child-Pugh A 1.1, B 0.7 mg/m2) and moderate/severe renal impairment (1.1 mg/m2)
Neutropenia is the dose-limiting toxicity - check CBC before every dose
Avoid in congenital long QT syndrome; correct potassium/magnesium and monitor ECG with other QT drugs
Do NOT dilute in or give through dextrose solutions, and do not mix with other drugs
missed: Not applicable for self-administration - eribulin is given by the oncology team on scheduled days (1 and 8) of each cycle. A delayed or missed dose is rescheduled per blood counts and clinical assessment.
overdose: Overdose at approximately 4 times the recommended dose produced Grade 3 neutropenia lasting 7 days and a Grade 3 hypersensitivity reaction lasting 1 day. There is no known antidote; manage with supportive care including monitoring and treatment of neutropenia and hypersensitivity.
